title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County are suing Española after police stopped them on July 23. A Flock Safety camera misread the license plate on Jaclynn Gonzales's car, reading a final 2 as a 7 and flagging it as stolen from Rio Rancho. Officers pulled over the 21-year-old and her 12-year-old sister on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate police cars before realizing the mistake. Jaclynn asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another vehicle.

The sisters filed lawsuits on January 3 seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was forced to kneel in the road with his hands on his head after a similar camera error in April. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits will proceed in state District Court, but no next steps or hearing dates are mentioned.
